text: End-of-semester and make-up theory papers can be submitted for re-evaluation. This service excludes supplementary exams and summer-term courses. Midterms, practicals, labs, assignments, projects, internships and viva assessments also fall outside the re-evaluation scope.

Students normally have 15 days from announcement of results to submit the prescribed re-evaluation form to the Controller of Examinations and pay the applicable fee. The manual lists a non-refundable charge of ₹5,000 for each subject, subject to changes in university policy. Incomplete forms can be rejected.

The Vice-Chancellor chooses an independent reviewer from a panel suggested by the Controller of Examinations. The reviewer receives a digital copy of the answer sheet with identifying details masked. If the first review differs from the original marks by over 20%, a different evaluator conducts another review and the two review scores are averaged.

Re-evaluation results appear in the ERP. Students cannot view the answer sheet after it has been re-evaluated. When revised marks call for a new grade sheet, the student must hand in the previous grade sheet.
The exam manual schedules issuance of both grade sheets and transcripts after 15 days from publication of the result.

The admissions scholarship page describes a limited pool allocated first come, first served. Meeting published criteria does not give an applicant a guaranteed scholarship. If several awards apply, the university grants the one with the greatest value under its guidelines.

On the public admissions scholarship page, the university states a continuation CGPA of 8 on a 10-point scale. Students who entered without an admission scholarship may qualify for a 10% academic scholarship, subject to the university policy.

The notice dated 17 June 2025 announced May 2025 even-semester results for other schools and semesters. The notice set 19 June 2025 as the result date for B.Tech CSE semesters 2 and 6. Students were directed to check their ERP account.

Programme-wise results for December 2024 end-term exams started appearing on 10 January 2025 and were released in phases. Students were asked to check ERP for updates. Odd semester make-up results were announced on 31 January 2025, and odd semester supplementary results on 4 March 2025.
Minimum course attendance across lectures, tutorials and labs: 75%. Grade for shortage of course attendance: DB. Attendance credit for each scheduled class regardless of its length: One unit.

Maximum exceptional attendance relaxation: Up to 10%. Continuous certified illness duration considered for attendance relaxation: Two weeks. Approval to represent the university for attendance relaxation: Prior approval of the Dean.
Authorisation for a personal-reason attendance exception: Dean recommendation and Vice-Chancellor approval.

Official who may allow a scribe on the Dean’s recommendation: Controller of Examinations. Exam venue for candidates using a scribe: A separate room or the wellness centre. Writing-hand injury criterion for scribe assistance: An injury that prevents writing.
Grade points for a C+: 6. Grade points for a D: 4. Grade points for an F: 0.
Lowest passing letter grade on the standard scale: D. Grade for failing a mandatory non-credit course: FF. Semesters covered by the CGPA: All completed semesters.

Final approval authority for moderated exam results: Vice-Chancellor. Portal on which faculty enter exam and assessment marks: ERP. Stage at which the grade report is generated: After grades are locked in the ERP.

Chair of the examination grievance committee: Controller of Examinations. Member secretary of the examination grievance committee: An office representative from the Controller of Examinations. Dedicated email for examination grievances: exam.grievance@bennett.edu.in.

University ticket system for examination grievances: BU Helpdesk. Channel used to acknowledge an exam grievance: The submission channel. Person asked to verify an allegedly out-of-syllabus question: Course coordinator.

Online platform for viewing assessed end-term sheets: Digital Valuation Platform. Appendix with the discrepancy-reporting form for viewed answer sheets: Appendix G. Listed non-refundable re-evaluation fee: ₹5,000 per subject, subject to policy changes.

Official who appoints the independent re-evaluation examiner: Vice-Chancellor. Copy sent to the independent re-evaluation examiner: An anonymised digital answer sheet. Where re-evaluation results are published: ERP.

Deadline to submit a mid-term make-up request with documents: Within five days of the last exam date. Additional medical opinion needed for illness-related make-up requests: University Medical Officer’s opinion. Final approver of a mid-term make-up request after Dean review: Vice-Chancellor.

Scheduled window for mid-term make-up exams: Between the mid-term and end-semester exams. Consequence of missing the make-up examination: No second make-up chance. Who sets the duration of a mid-term make-up exam: Faculty or course coordinator.
Who notifies approved mid-term make-up cases: Dean Academic. Initial result for an approved missed end-semester exam: I grade. Mandatory assessment for any project-course grade: Final viva.

Regular-exam failure group eligible for a supplementary exam: Students with an F in the regular exam. What determines supplementary eligibility after disciplinary exclusion: Outcome of disciplinary proceedings and university rules. Where the supplementary registration deadline is listed: Academic Calendar.

Exam route for backlog courses in a one-year programme: Special supplementary examination. Non-refundable supplementary fee for batches starting in 2024–25: ₹3,000 per course, subject to change. Frequency of regular supplementary exams for recently completed semesters: Twice in an academic year.

Next chance after failing a supplementary exam: The next corresponding odd or even supplementary exam. Standard period for clearing failures through supplementary exams: Normal programme duration plus two years. Discretionary authority for the mercy attempt after N+2: Vice-Chancellor.

Attendance needed by debarred students for remedial classes: At least 50% attendance. Length of a supplementary exam compared with the regular end term: Same duration as the end-term exam. Treatment of internal marks in a supplementary exam: Existing internal marks are retained.

Supplementary provision for mid-term exams and internal assessments: No supplementary option. Pass requirement for supplementary exams: Same passing mark as end term. Highest possible supplementary exam grade: C+.
Maximum special supplementary registration load: 24 credits.

Approval for summer term registration after first year: School Dean’s permission. Prior attempts required for summer term from year two: Two supplementary attempts in the same subject. Summer term registration limit: 15 credits or five courses.

Documents needed for examination hall entry: University ID card and admit card. Office issuing temporary or duplicate university IDs before exams: Registrar’s Office. When to request a replacement university ID before exams: One week in advance.

CGPA route for progression from the end of the second year onward: 4.0 on a 10-point scale. Credit-based alternative to the CGPA route from the end of year two: All prior-year credits and 50% of current-year credits. Certified medical absence requiring compulsory semester withdrawal: At least five weeks.
Grade for compulsory medical semester withdrawal: W.

Sibling scholarship rate and duration: 10% during programme overlap. Relationship required for the sibling award: Children of the same parents. Single girl child scholarship amount and duration: 10% of tuition throughout the programme.

Award for Bennett alumni enrolling in a Bennett postgraduate programme: 10% of tuition. Maximum sport-based admission scholarship on the public page: Up to 50% of first-year tuition. Sports participation or achievement levels considered: State, national or international level.
Scholarship for eligible wards of defence personnel: 5% of tuition for the full programme. Service status covered by the defence wards scholarship: Serving and retired personnel.

Class XII or CUET threshold for the 50% CSE Global award: 96 or higher. JEE Main percentile threshold for the 50% CSE Global award: 90 or higher. SAT threshold for the 50% CSE Global award: 1401 or higher.
IB score range for the 30% CSE Global award: 34–39. JEE Main range for the 20% CSE Global award: 70–74.99. SAT range for the 10% CSE Global award: 1201–1300.
Compulsory subjects in the CSE Global best-of-three calculation: Physics and mathematics. Non-CGPA renewal conditions for CSE Global admission awards: No backlog or recorded disciplinary case.

Publication date for the December 2025 odd-semester end-term results: 11 January 2026. Result announcement date for the August–September 2025 special supplementary exams: 12 September 2025. Result date announced for July 2025 summer-term exams: 8 August 2025.

Result date of the even-semester supplementary exams for 2023–24: 24 August 2024. Result date of the even-semester make-up exams for 2023–24: 19 July 2024. Result announcement for May 2024 regular even-semester exams: 4 June 2024.
Result date of regular odd-semester exams for 2023–24: 15 January 2024.
